central_thesis: Gong moved from educating the market on a new category ('Revenue Intelligence') to owning platform-level infrastructure identity ('Revenue AI OS') by replacing its explanatory H1 with a prediction-focused AI value prop and removing all educational navigation that previously onboarded buyers to the RI concept.
old_positioning_frame: A specialized sales tool that captures and analyzes conversations to help sales teams generate more revenue through better interactions ('Revenue Intelligence platform for sales optimization')
new_positioning_frame: An operating system-level platform that powers entire go-to-market organizations through multimodal AI processing, agents, and applications ('Revenue AI OS helps your entire GTM organization win')
buyer_shift: VP of Sales and sales team leads seeking conversation analytics → C-suite and revenue operations leaders purchasing cross-functional GTM infrastructure
funnel_shift: Mid-funnel education (explaining what Revenue Intelligence is and why sales teams need it) → Early-funnel category leadership and late-funnel enterprise validation (demonstrating platform maturity and enterprise adoption)

main_evidence.new: Revenue AI Built To Predict churnPredict churn
main_evidence.meaning: Signals a shift from category education to concrete, outcome-focused AI capabilities — the new H1 leads with a specific prediction use case rather than defining an abstract category, suggesting confidence that buyers already understand the problem space

main_evidence.old: Generate more revenue by having better sales conversations with the #1 revenue intelligence platform for sales optimization.
main_evidence.new: Gong Revenue AI OS helps your entire GTM organization win. Drive growth with multimodal revenue signal processing, specialized AI agents, and purpose-built applications.
main_evidence.meaning: Points to an expansion from sales-specific tool positioning to enterprise platform infrastructure — the introduction of 'OS' terminology and 'entire GTM organization' language is consistent with repositioning as foundational technology rather than departmental software

main_evidence.meaning: Suggests the company no longer needs to educate visitors on the category concept — removing 'What is RI?' and the educational podcast while adding product-specific and innovation-focused navigation may indicate the market has matured past the awareness stage

main_evidence.meaning: Indicates a shift from explaining product functionality to validating enterprise adoption — the new headings lead with social proof scale and named enterprise case studies rather than feature education, which is consistent with targeting later-stage, risk-averse enterprise buyers

main_evidence.new: Read the case study · Learn about our product · View more customer stories
main_evidence.meaning: Suggests a move from individual practitioner testimonials to formal enterprise validation materials — replacing named VP quotes with structured case studies may signal positioning for procurement processes that require documented ROI rather than peer influence

copy_this_if: Your product category has reached the 'Gartner Magic Quadrant' stage where analysts define your space, competitors explicitly position against you, and enterprise RFPs list your category by name in requirements documents
do_not_copy_this_if: Prospects still ask 'what does your product do?' in discovery calls, or you need to explain your product category using analogies to existing tools
safer_version_for_early_stage_saas: Keep your category-defining term in the H1 ('Revenue Intelligence') but test adding a concrete prediction outcome in the subheader ('Built to predict churn, identify upsells, and forecast deals') — this educates on the category while proving immediate AI value without requiring buyers to already know what your category means
risk_if_copied: Buyers who don't yet understand the problem space will interpret 'Revenue AI OS' as vague enterprise buzzwords and bounce to competitors who clearly explain what the software does and which specific pain it solves — particularly dangerous if your sales team still spends the first 10 minutes of demos explaining the category
